reason: At base the object JIT fastpass only guards issue-concat with presence, so a superRefine that writes ctx.value alongside a swallowed issue lands {a:"leaked"} in a successful parse of {}; the test expects no key for the absent property.

At head the JIT codegen guards both issues and value assignment on !issues.length || present, matching the interpreted path: absent key yields no key in output and present key with failing check reports failure.

At base marked paragraph continuation lookahead only treats spaces-only lines as blank, so foo\n\t\nbar renders as one

foo\tbar

instead of two paragraphs.
At head the paragraph rule accepts [ \t]+\n as blank, so a tab-only line separates foo and bar into two distinct paragraphs.

The PR only touches error-path stack decoration in Axios.prototype.request; default transformResponse already parses application/json bodies into objects at base, so a successful GET resolves data as an object.
Success path is untouched by this error-handling fix, and default response transformation still parses JSON bodies into objects at head.
A plain --verbose boolean flag parses normally at base; the negative-number regex fix only affects args like -1E3, not ordinary flags.
The uppercase-E regex change does not affect plain flag parsing; --verbose still reads true with no unknown-option error at head.
At base JsonTreeReader.nextInt() lacks ASCII validation and Integer.parseInt silently coerces full-width digits U+FF11FF13 to 123, so no parsing error is raised.
At head nextInt()/nextLong() call validateAscii on string tokens and throw MalformedJsonException for non-ASCII digits, exactly what the test expects.
At base, parseSearchPath uses allowlist regex [a-zA-z0-9$] that excludes '-', so 'test-db' is split into 'test' and 'db' instead of one schema name.
At head the regex is a delimiter blocklist ([^\s,"']), so 'test-db' stays a single schema name as expected.
The PR only changes ByteBufferUtil buffer recycling; Glide's default behavior of applying configured transformations when not disabled is unaffected at base.
The ByteBufferUtil leak fix does not touch request options or transformation logic, so transformations remain applied by default at head.
This is a pure caching refactor of allowedSymbolsAndAlphanumerics; at base the computed union behaves identically, so configured allowed symbols still suppress violations.
The cached CharacterSet is refreshed via didSet when allowedSymbols changes, preserving exact prior behavior, so identifiers using allowed symbols pass.
The PR only adds <cstdint> for compilation and cannot affect runtime data-URI handling; percent-encoded SVG data URIs load normally at base.
Arrow performs aware-datetime arithmetic via relativedelta, giving 10 absolute hours from 18:30 CST -> 05:30 CDT (-05:00); the Afrikaans-locale PR is unrelated.
The include-only compile fix cannot change runtime behavior, so percent-encoded SVG data URIs still load at head.
The PR touches only HTTPCookies directive parsing; Vapor's urlencoded form decoding of an empty body into an all-optional Decodable already succeeds at base.
Cookie-header parsing changes are unrelated to content decoding, which still yields an all-nil instance for an empty urlencoded body.
The PR only fixes spelling in comments/tests; afero's mem filesystem already refuses to remove non-empty directories with an error at base.
Spelling-only changes cannot alter Remove() semantics; the mem filesystem still rejects removing non-empty directories.
The PR only fixes a json_encode depth argument in JsonTest; schema comparison handling of equally-matching index renames is unaffected at base.
Same trivial test-only change; the comparator behavior for duplicate equivalent indexes is unchanged at head.
The Afrikaans locale addition is unrelated to shift(); aware-datetime arithmetic yields 05:30 with -05:00 offset at base.

The PR only touches CircuitBreakerStateMachine predicate handling, which is unrelated to the semaphore RateLimiter under test. The test's wording ('rather than permanently stopping all further admissions') indicates it reproduces a known base-revision bug where lowering limitForPeriod below accumulated permits halts replenishment, so it fails at base.

Same rate-limiter replenishment test as kb_0011 but executed after a PR that only modifies CircuitBreakerStateMachine; the RateLimiter code is unchanged, so the pre-existing stop-replenishing bug remains and the test still fails.

The PR touches only prefer-template, unrelated to no-var. At base, no-var's autofix rewrites 'var a = 1;' to a block-scoped declaration without guarding references that occur before the declaration, so the preceding foo() call reads 'a' in the temporal dead zone and throws ReferenceError instead of printing undefined.

Same no-var autofix scenario as kbc_0001, executed after a PR that only modifies prefer-template; the no-var fixer still rewrites 'var count = 5;' to block-scoped syntax, so schedule(printCount) invoked before the declaration hits the temporal dead zone and throws instead of printing undefined.

The PR only changes logformatter_adapter in scrapy/utils/log.py, which has no bearing on scheduler persistence. JOBDIR-based resume of request queue, dupefilter, and spider state is established Scrapy behavior already working at base, so a restarted SitemapSpider continues crawling remaining sitemap URLs.

Same JOBDIR resume scenario as kbc_0003 but at head; the applied PR only alters log message argument handling in scrapy/utils/log.py and cannot affect scheduler persistence or spider closing behavior, so the resumed run still crawls remaining sitemap pages before finishing.

The PR only extends --sanitize's bidi handling and cannot affect wrapping or highlighting. At base, bat still has the capacity-overflow family of bugs around --terminal-width 1 (the repo changelog shows sibling fixes), and printing a double-width character with a highlighted background at width 1 with character wrap triggers such a panic rather than exiting cleanly.

The head revision only adds bidi codepoints to --sanitize; the wrapping/highlighting printer is untouched. The base's capacity-overflow weakness when rendering content wider than --terminal-width 1 (sibling fixes for it already appear in the changelog) still applies to double-width characters under a row-filling theme, so bat panics instead of exiting 0.

The PR only touches the RFC5424 syslog regexp, which is unrelated to out_file. At base, chunking by the key field puts aa and bb records into separate buffer chunks, and out_file's write() extracts placeholders per-chunk metadata and creates each symlink, so both symlinks exist after the flush.

Same out_file symlink scenario as kbc_0011 executed at head; the applied PR changes only the syslog parser regexp and cannot affect per-chunk placeholder extraction or symlink updates, so the follow-up record's chunk flush still refreshes that key's symlink.

The PR modifies only ConcurrentBag yield behavior, not pool naming. Generating the default pool name uses an atomic counter rather than reading/writing system properties, so concurrent System-properties activity elsewhere cannot block pool construction even before the change.

Same scenario as kbc_0013 executed at head; the PR only alters ConcurrentBag's yield/park behavior and pool-name generation still relies on an atomic counter with no lock shared with System-properties access, so concurrent pool construction completes without deadlock.

The PR only fixes the SORT STORE ACL keyspec parsing and cannot affect persistence. The test's emphasis on a 32-bit build succeeding only 'past a few megabytes' indicates it reproduces a base-revision 32-bit RDB/BGSAVE defect where background saves of multi-megabyte datasets terminate with an error rather than reporting rdb_last_bgsave_status:ok.

Same 32-bit background-save scenario as kbd_0001 executed after a PR confined to sortGetKeys ACL parsing; nothing in the diff touches rdb saving or signal handling on 32-bit builds, so the size-dependent save failure at base persists and the log will not show a clean 'terminated successfully'.

The PR only touches directory-context save/restore in context.c, unrelated to do_addsub in ops.c. At base Neovim increments decimal numbers with arbitrary-precision string arithmetic rather than wrapping at 64 bits, so the 50-digit literal becomes exactly +1 with every digit preserved.

Same arbitrary-precision increment/decrement behavior as kbd_0003, executed at head; the applied PR only fixes CWD bookkeeping in context.c and cannot alter do_addsub, so CTRL-X decrements the 50-digit number by exactly one.

The PR only changes external file cache block retirement, which cannot affect the binder. At base, '||' on lists binds through the SQLNULL pseudo-type so the untyped NULL casts to the array operand's type, returning an INTEGER[] column containing NULL rather than a scalar.

Same binder-level behavior as kbd_0005 evaluated at head; the applied PR only touches external file cache retirement and cannot influence operator or function type resolution, so '||' and list_concat both report INTEGER[] for a list concatenated with NULL.

The PR modifies only ScrollBar drag-scroll input handling, unrelated to object lifetime. At base, RefCounted's final unreference triggers _predelete which delivers NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE through to the GDScript instance while the object and its members are still valid, so the override runs and reads the member without crashing.

Same RefCounted PREDELETE scenario as kbd_0007 executed at head; the applied PR touches only ScrollBar touch-drag handling and cannot affect object destruction, so the handler still reads the assigned member value and the engine exits cleanly.

The PR only adds a ValueError for categorical features with criterion='absolute_error' in trees, unrelated to feature_selection. At base, f_regression defaults to force_finite=True, which maps an undefined correlation from a constant column to F=0.0 and p=1.0 with no sqrt/divide RuntimeWarning.

The PR only affects tree categorical-feature validation, not feature_selection. A column differing in its last significant digits still has strictly positive variance, so r_regression's Pearson computation produces a normal finite correlation without triggering any invalid-sqrt or divide RuntimeWarning.

The PR only fixes the Vault UI's swagger-ui component and cannot affect agent sinks. The file sink's 'mode' configuration option is long-supported at base and its chmod is applied when the token file is written, so the resulting permissions are 640 as configured.

Same file sink scenario as kbd_0011 executed at head; the applied PR changes only the UI's swagger component and cannot touch sink file handling, so mode = 0600 still yields owner-only rw------- permissions on the token file.

At base, Click appends the default options metavar so a command with no parameters prints 'Usage: cli [OPTIONS]', not exactly 'Usage: cli'; additionally the pre-fix write_usage dropped the prefix entirely when args was empty (#3360). The PR only fixes the formatter edge case and does not remove [OPTIONS], so the expected first line does not match.

Even at head, a command that does not customize its usage metavar still renders 'Usage: cli [OPTIONS]' for --help (the PR's own end-to-end tests reach bare 'Usage: cli' only via options_metavar='' / None), so the exact expected first line is not produced.

The PR only changes host/port parsing in app.run and the test client's session helper, unrelated to response conversion. At base, returning a dict from a view is jsonified by the default provider with Content-Type application/json and compact separators.

Same dict-view JSON behavior as py_0007 evaluated at head; the applied PR only alters IPv6 host parsing for the dev server and test client sessions, leaving the jsonify conversion of returned dictionaries untouched.

The PR only changes how deprecated typing aliases are matched during schema generation for unhashable generic aliases, which cannot affect field-requiredness. At base, constructing a model while omitting a field without a default raises a ValidationError listing that field as missing.

Same required-field omission behavior as py_0009 evaluated at head; the applied PR only affects alias matching for unhashable generic aliases during schema generation and leaves model field validation unchanged.

The PR only renames logging.WARN to the numerically identical logging.WARNING in setup code and docs, changing no behavior. At base, the sqlalchemy root logger defaults to WARNING so INFO-level SQL records are suppressed when echo is off and emitted when echo is turned on.

Same echo-suppression scenario as py_0011 evaluated at head; the PR's WARN-to-WARNING rename is value-identical and behavior-neutral, so INFO SQL logging is still filtered out with echo off and present with echo on.

At base, once attribute methods are generated the aliased computed attribute falls through a cheap flag-checking method_missing into the normal attribute reader, adding only a few stack frames over a real column read, so the measured ratio stays below the ~20x bound.

Unlike base, the new always-suspect method_missing runs its whole slow path on each computed-attribute read: a define_attribute_methods call plus public_instance_method lookup that rescues a NameError per invocation before delegating. That added per-call overhead pushes the computed-vs-column read ratio past the ~20x bound.

At base, preProcess pushes a fresh WrappedListener onto the call stack on every dispatch and called listeners are never removed from it during postProcess (the leak), so getCalledListeners reports one entry per invocation and counts two after two dispatches.

At head, postProcess records each called listener into calledListenerInfos only when its original is not already present for that event, so dispatching twice with one listener yields exactly one entry from getCalledListeners instead of the expected per-invocation count of two.

The PR only reworks how compgen output populates COMPREPLY and adds a popd guard for shellcheck compliance; at base the generated script's per-subcommand custom completion handlers are invoked based on the active command in the line and return their own dynamic values, so each sibling subcommand suggests only its own values.

The shellcheck-driven changes preserve semantics for the exercised path: on a plain post-subcommand noun Tab, COMPREPLY starts out empty so the switch from assignment to appending behaves identically, and the per-subcommand custom hooks still see last_command set to the active subcommand, returning their own scoped suggestions.

At base (qs 6.13.0), repeating an unbracketed key appends every value to an array with no length restriction; the 20-entry arrayLimit only governs explicit numeric indices like ids[21]. All 25 values therefore parse into an in-order array under the default extended query parser.

Same scenario as rg_0011 after the qs 6.13.0 -> 6.14.0 bump; that release makes no change to the default duplicates=combine behavior for unbracketed repeated keys, so all 25 values still parse into an in-order array.
At base get_environ_proxies has the single-parameter signature get_environ_proxies(url), so calling it with only the URL succeeds and returns the environment proxy dict (empty when none apply).

The PR changes the signature to get_environ_proxies(url, no_proxy) without a default, so calling it with only the URL now raises TypeError: missing required positional argument 'no_proxy' instead of returning a proxy dict.

At base, parse_unit_value only engages for tokens starting with an ASCII digit or '-' followed by one, so '.foons' falls through to ordinary bare-word parsing; [.foons] | get 0 yields the string '.foons' with no parser error.

At head the relaxed guard admits '.foons' into parse_unit_value, which splits off a unit-like suffix and fails to parse '.' as a number, returning a parse error result instead of falling back to bare-word string parsing, so [.foons] | get 0 errors rather than returning '.foons'.

This case reproduces guzzle/guzzle#2741: at base the curl handler still attaches a sink/write callback for HEAD requests, and with an Accept-Encoding default header the transfer aborts with a curl error instead of returning a response. Only after this PR are sinks skipped for HEAD.

At head the curl handler skips sink and write-callback setup entirely for HEAD requests (the fix for #2741), so a HEAD request carrying Accept-Encoding completes normally and yields a response instead of aborting.

At base, ExUnit's diff renderer lacks the robust handling later added around this era for irregular container contents; rendering the failure message for %{bar: [1 | 2]} raises a FunctionClauseError in the algebra/safe_to_algebra traversal instead of printing a clean 'match (=) failed' report.

The PR only converts inserted/deleted maps to AST form for equality-diff contexts; in match-context assertions like this one escaping is bypassed and the improper-list traversal that crashes the formatter at base is unchanged, so the failure message still cannot be produced without an internal error.

This is exactly the css-props-dynamic-component scenario the PR adds a regression test for; at base the dynamic component path mis-hydrates css_props (wrong anchor resolution and the stale teardown removing elements), so after toggling, the inner component loses its --prop styling or hydration errors occur instead of staying red.

At head the fix is in place: dynamic Component nodes compile through the same $.component hydration path as <svelte:component>, css_props no longer removes its element on teardown, and this is precisely the sample test added with the PR asserting red both before and after the toggle.

At base there is no transform.code filter; the handler only requires the code to contain 'new URL' and 'import.meta.url', and assetImportMetaUrlRE matches across newlines because its separators are \s*. The multi-line reference is therefore rewritten to the emitted asset URL just like the single-line form.

At head the transform gains a hook filter code: /new\s+URL.+import\.meta\.url/ whose dot does not match newlines; in the multi-line form 'import.meta.url' sits on a later line than 'new URL', the filter rejects the module, the plugin's handler never runs, and the worker asset is neither emitted nor rewritten.

At base the preview child environment never includes the item text, so the NUL bytes in the delimiter-split item cannot poison exec; the preview command spawns via the shell and displays its output without any child-process-start error.

At head the preview child environment gains FZF_CURRENT_ITEM set to the raw item text; the current item contains a NUL byte from the delimiter-split line, and Go's os/exec refuses environment entries containing NUL, so starting the preview command fails and fzf reports an error instead of showing 'ok'.

At base, enabling EDGE_TO_EDGE assigns layout-only SYSTEM_UI_FLAG_* values and pushes them through setSystemUiVisibility, replacing the immersive-sticky hide flags wholesale, so the status and navigation bars become visible again after the switch.

At head, entering edge-to-edge returns early after WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows(false), which only affects insets and does not touch bar visibility; nothing replaces the immersive-sticky hide flags left by step 1, so the status and navigation bars remain hidden instead of reappearing.
At base the MultipleCaseAssignment semantic check does not exist, so nothing flags the class pattern whose keyword name equals its capture name; the file checks cleanly under --preview.

The new MatchClass handling inserts keyword.attr and then also inserts the capture-name from visiting keyword.pattern; for case ClassLabel(num_classes=num_classes) both are the identifier 'num_classes', so the checker emits a spurious 'multiple assignments to name' syntax error under --preview instead of passing cleanly.

At base, decodeBlockToValue indexes the destination slice without growing it; with one placeholder entry and two nested blocks, the second write uses index 1 on a length-1 slice and panics with slice index out of range instead of producing a two-entry list.

At head the decoder appends a new element whenever the block index exceeds the current slice length before decoding into it, so two nested blocks decode into a grown two-entry slice without panicking, matching the regression test added in this PR.

At base, mockConstructorParameters only calls setTimezone when an explicit timezone argument is given; mocking with an America/Los_Angeles moment therefore leaves 'now' carrying that zone, and Carbon::now() formats in Los Angeles time instead of the UTC default the test expects.

At head, the mocked instance is always re-set to $timezone ?? date_default_timezone_get(), so with UTC as the default and no explicit mock timezone, Carbon::now() renders the mocked moment in UTC exactly as testTimezoneConsistency (added by this PR) asserts.

At base the protocol-relative regexp is ^[/\\]{2}[^/\\]+, which requires exactly two adjacent slashes and a non-slash afterwards; '///test.com', '/<TAB>//test.com' and '/\/test.com' all fail it and are not reported protocol-relative, contradicting all three expectations this PR's expanded regex fixes.

At head the regex is ^([/\\]\s*){2,}[^/\\], which accepts three-plus slashes with optional whitespace between them and mixed slash types, so '///test.com', '/<TAB>//test.com' and '/\/test.com' are all classified as protocol-relative with no explicit protocol, matching the new test entries.

The PR only swaps a defensive-copy accessor for an internal one in hash-combining helpers and cannot alter hashing results. Guava's md5().hashString("abc", UTF_8) has always produced the standard digest 900150983cd24fb0d6963f7d28e17f72.

Same MD5 sanity scenario as sa_0009 at head; the applied change is copy-elision inside combine helpers with zero effect on Hashing.md5() output, so the digest for "abc" is still the standard 900150983cd24fb0d6963f7d28e17f72.

The PR is a pure code-motion refactor of diagnostic descriptors with identical codes and messages; at base, generating a client for an interface method annotated with a GET attribute is core, well-tested Refit functionality that emits a working implementation issuing a GET to the route.

Same GET-generation scenario as sa_0011 at head; the applied PR only relocates diagnostic descriptors into a new static class without changing generation logic, so the generated client still issues the expected GET request.

The PR removes only provably redundant continue statements with no change in control flow; at base a plain HTTP/1.1 GET against a fixed-content-length test server is hyper's most fundamental exercised path and returns the exact configured body.

Same plain HTTP/1.1 GET scenario as sa_0013 evaluated at head; the applied PR only deletes control-flow-equivalent continue statements, leaving h1 request/response handling untouched and the fixed body returned intact.

At base, the custom-calendar clause of Date.to_iso8601/2 converts to Calendar.ISO and then calls the zero-arity to_iso8601(), discarding the requested format; for a Holocene date the :basic call therefore returns '2001-01-01' instead of '20010101'.

At head the format argument is threaded through the ISO conversion, so a Holocene date formatted with :basic returns '20010101' while the default call still yields '2001-01-01', exactly as the regression test added in this PR asserts.

At base, setEndDate updates Carbon's internal endDate but never re-synchronizes the native DatePeriod 'end' property, which PHP 8.2+ manages internally; reading $period->end therefore still returns 2024-09-30 while getEndDate() returns 2025-06-15.

At head, setEndDate finishes by calling syncNativePeriod(), which re-invokes parent DatePeriod::__construct so the native 'end' property reflects 2025-06-15; both the property and getEndDate() now agree with the regression test added in this PR.

At base there is no whitespace validation in Request#headline or the host header; with a pass-through normalizer the client happily builds a request line containing the embedded newline and transmits it, instead of raising the 'Invalid request URI' error this PR introduces.

At head, Request#headline raises RequestError 'Invalid request URI: "/hello\nworld"' when the request URI contains whitespace, before anything is transmitted, which is precisely the regression spec added with this PR.
The PR only adds a pluralName to the Albanian locale data; English number-to-words conversion is untouched and has long produced 'one million' and 'two million' at base.
Same English words-conversion scenario as sb_0007 at head; the applied PR touches only the Albanian locale YAML and its tests, leaving default English output as 'one million' and 'two million'.

The PR only changes how java.util.Properties entries are loaded into Koin's property registry; singleton-scoped definition resolution is untouched core behavior, so resolving the same component twice at base returns one identical instance.

Same singleton-resolution scenario as sb_0009 evaluated at head; the applied PR only relaxes property-map type handling in PropertyRegistryExt and cannot affect instance scoping, so both resolutions still yield the same object.

At base, OrderedDictionary.replaceElement(at:) swaps in the new key while preserving order and traps via precondition 'Duplicate key' when the replacement key already exists, so both parts of the expected outcome hold before this behavior-preserving refactor.

Same replace-element scenario as sb_0011 evaluated at head; the shared _replaceNew primitive performs the identical append/swap/remove sequence and the duplicate-key precondition is still checked before any mutation, so order is preserved and duplicates still trap.

At base, cast.ToInt("-5MB") fails to parse and yields 0 (and a purely numeric negative like -5 would be clamped by the explicit if size < 0 check), so the size accessor already returns 0 bytes for this invalid value before the max() refactor.
Same size-parsing scenario as sb_0013 at head; max(cast.ToInt("-5MB"), 0) is behaviorally identical to the removed clamp, returning 0 for the unparseable string.

This reproduces gin#2959: at base, findCaseInsensitivePathRec grabs children[0] when wildChild is set, but the wildcard child is appended last, so a node holding both /prefix/xxx and /prefix/:id makes the mis-cased lookup hit the static child in the wildcard switch and panic 'invalid node type' instead of resolving or returning not-found.

At head, findCaseInsensitivePathRec tries static children via indices first and only falls back to children[len-1] (the actual wildcard child), so /PREFIX/XXX resolves to /prefix/xxx and unmatched /prefix/a/b/c returns not-found without the invalid-node-type panic, as the new regression tests demonstrate.

At base, Int64Value on a valid-but-empty Numeric goes through toBigInt, which returns the nil Int when Exp==0, and the subsequent IsInt64 dereference panics with a nil pointer instead of reporting zero like Float64Value does.
At head, toBigInt returns big.NewInt(0) when Int is nil, so Int64Value reports zero without panicking and agrees with Float64Value, matching the regression test added in this PR.

The PR only changes terminal tab-stop handling in the renderer and cannot affect the event loop. Calling Quit from another goroutine is a documented, long-supported Bubbletea pattern that unblocks Run and makes it return nil shortly after.

Same external-quit scenario as sys_0005 evaluated at head; the applied PR only adjusts tab-stop escape sequences in the renderer, leaving the quit/event-loop machinery unchanged so Run still returns promptly after an external Quit.

At base, RunUntilCancelledFuture polls the wrapped future before consulting the cancellation signal, so with an already-cancelled token the first poll executes the inner async block, which panics ('fut polled after cancellation') instead of resolving to Ready(None) untouched.

At head, run_until_cancelled checks self.is_cancelled() before constructing the combined future and returns None immediately, so the panicking inner future is never polled — exactly the regression test this PR adds.

The PR only skips parsing ignore files in directories whose children cannot be visited; matcher case handling is untouched, and ripgrep's -i/--ignore-case search has reported matches of any letter casing at base.

Same case-insensitive search scenario as sys_0009 evaluated at head; the applied PR only avoids loading ignore files in unreachable directories, leaving the matcher and its case-insensitivity fully intact.

At base, serde's derive already initializes skip_deserializing fields to Default::default() when no container-level default exists; the PR is an equivalent restatement of this very condition, so an omitted skipped field still reads as the type's zero value.

Same skip_deserializing scenario as sys_0011 evaluated at head; the PR only flattens the nested if into a single boolean conjunction with identical semantics, so the skipped field still receives Default::default().
